important_findings: Lagged unemployment was the strongest predictive signal.
Economic-demographic predictors did not improve temporal validation accuracy over the Lag-Only Linear Regression model.
Adding CPI inflation did not improve average predictive performance on the common CPI-covered sample.
The Persistence Baseline slightly outperformed Linear Regression on the final unseen 2023-24 test period.
Prediction errors tended to increase for observations with higher unemployment rates.
limitations: The model is designed for short-horizon State-level unemployment estimation.
Predictions depend strongly on the previous observed unemployment rate.
The model should not be interpreted as establishing causal relationships.
Sudden State-level unemployment changes and extreme unemployment values are more difficult to predict.
The model is not designed for long-horizon forecasting without additional future information.
